rubric:
# Rubric for judging a flag

You are given flags that Redline showed a reader. Each flag names a clause type and
quotes one sentence from an agreement, with the paragraph around it. Judge each flag
on its own against this rubric, and nothing else.

## The rule

**PASS** if the quoted sentence really is the kind of clause the flag names and really
costs the reader something. Otherwise **FAIL**.

Both halves have to hold. A sentence that costs the reader something but isn't the
kind of clause the flag names is a FAIL. So is a sentence that is the kind of clause
the flag names but costs the reader nothing.

## Who the reader is

From `PRD.md`:

> Redline reads a document someone is about to be bound by and tells them what it
> actually says.

The reader is the person being asked to sign. "The other side" is the party that
wrote the agreement.

## What a flag is, and the clause types

`PRD.md` doesn't define clause types by name. Each flag names its own type in a few
plain words, and the first half of the rule asks whether the quoted sentence is a
clause of that type, in the ordinary meaning of the words the flag uses. Read the
sentence in its paragraph. The paragraph can show what the sentence refers to, but the
sentence is the one being judged.

What the PRD says a flag is:

> **Flag** — a clause capable of harming the reader.

And what it says separates a clause worth flagging from one that is merely unusual:

> Use the dangerous-vs-unusual test from ADR-0004: a clause that lets the other side
> change the reader's economics unilaterally after the reader is committed is
> dangerous; a non-standard but symmetric clause is not, and gets dropped rather than
> ranked low.

## What "costs the reader something" means

The PRD measures cost by consequence:

> **Severity** ranks what the item costs the reader if it fires, not how often it
> fires (ADR-0004).

A sentence costs the reader something when, if what it allows happens, the reader
ends up worse off: money paid or lost, a right given up, or something they now have to
do or may not do. How likely that is doesn't matter. Whether it happens is enough.

## Edge cases

None are settled yet. The labeller's notes are empty, so there is nothing to turn into
a general rule.

## Not part of the rule

- **Severity.** The flag's number is shown, but whether it is too high or too low
  doesn't change PASS or FAIL.
- **Whether the quote is in the document.** Code already checks that every quoted
  sentence appears in the agreement word for word. Take the quote as given.
- **Enforceability.** Whether a court would uphold the clause, and what the law
  somewhere requires, are not part of the rule.

## What to return

For each flag, its number, PASS or FAIL, and one sentence on why.

flags.sourceSentence: An amount not paid by the due date shown on the bill incurs a late payment charge of the greater of five dollars ($5.00) or one and one half percent of the unpaid balance, applied each bill period until the balance is paid, and a restored line incurs the restoral charge shown in the Rate and Charge Guide.
flags.paragraph: An amount not paid by the due date shown on the bill incurs a late payment charge of the greater of five dollars ($5.00) or one and one half percent of the unpaid balance, applied each bill period until the balance is paid, and a restored line incurs the restoral charge shown in the Rate and Charge Guide.

flags.sourceSentence: Charges accrue to the end of the bill period in which you cancel, and a part bill period is not prorated.
flags.paragraph: You may cancel a line at any time by calling us or through the account portal. Charges accrue to the end of the bill period in which you cancel, and a part bill period is not prorated.

flags.sourceSentence: The Firm may amend the Programme Handbook, the assessment structure, the teaching schedule and the terms of this Agreement at any time by issuing a revised version to the Analyst by email, and the revised version applies from the date of that email.
flags.paragraph: The Firm may amend the Programme Handbook, the assessment structure, the teaching schedule and the terms of this Agreement at any time by issuing a revised version to the Analyst by email, and the revised version applies from the date of that email.

flags.sourceSentence: The Analyst will indemnify the Firm and hold it harmless against any claim, loss or expense, including reasonable legal costs, arising out of a breach by the Analyst of Section 4 or Section 5, or out of anything the Analyst publishes about the Firm or a client of the Firm.
flags.paragraph: The Analyst will indemnify the Firm and hold it harmless against any claim, loss or expense, including reasonable legal costs, arising out of a breach by the Analyst of Section 4 or Section 5, or out of anything the Analyst publishes about the Firm or a client of the Firm.

flags.sourceSentence: For six (6) months after the Programme ends, the Analyst will not accept an engagement, whether paid or unpaid and whether as an employee, a contractor or an intern, with any firm on the Restricted List issued to the Analyst in week one of the Programme, and will not approach any client of the Firm whose file the Analyst worked on.
flags.paragraph: For six (6) months after the Programme ends, the Analyst will not accept an engagement, whether paid or unpaid and whether as an employee, a contractor or an intern, with any firm on the Restricted List issued to the Analyst in week one of the Programme, and will not approach any client of the Firm whose file the Analyst worked on.

flags.sourceSentence: The Firm may end the Programme early for any reason on one week written notice.
flags.paragraph: The Programme is a fixed term engagement and carries no offer or promise of further employment. The Firm may end the Programme early for any reason on one week written notice.

flags.sourceSentence: Any dispute between the Analyst and the Firm arising out of the Programme or out of this Agreement will be resolved by final and binding arbitration on an individual basis, administered under the employment rules of a nationally recognised provider, and the Analyst gives up any right to a jury trial and any right to bring or join a class or collective action.
flags.paragraph: Any dispute between the Analyst and the Firm arising out of the Programme or out of this Agreement will be resolved by final and binding arbitration on an individual basis, administered under the employment rules of a nationally recognised provider, and the Analyst gives up any right to a jury trial and any right to bring or join a class or collective action.

flags.sourceSentence: and any instalment not recovered within ten (10) days of its due date carries the late charge set out in the Programme Handbook until it is repaid in full.
flags.paragraph: Where the Analyst takes the optional housing advance, it is repaid in six equal instalments deducted from the stipend, and any instalment not recovered within ten (10) days of its due date carries the late charge set out in the Programme Handbook until it is repaid in full.

flags.sourceSentence: An item not returned within five working days is charged at the replacement cost shown in the Programme Handbook.
flags.paragraph: The laptop, the security token and the building pass issued to the Analyst remain the property of the Firm and are returned on the last day of the Programme. An item not returned within five working days is charged at the replacement cost shown in the Programme Handbook.

flags.sourceSentence: This obligation has no end date.
flags.paragraph: The Analyst will keep confidential every client name, model, memorandum and data set the Analyst sees during the Programme, and will not retain a copy of any of it after the Programme ends. This obligation has no end date.

flags.sourceSentence: The volunteer will treat borrower records as confidential and will not discuss what any named person has borrowed.
flags.paragraph: The volunteer will treat borrower records as confidential and will not discuss what any named person has borrowed.

flags.clauseType: Refund tiers on giving up a place
flags.sourceSentence: A place given up later than that, and before the third lesson, is refunded at half the fee.
flags.paragraph: A place given up more than seven days before the first lesson is refunded in full. A place given up later than that, and before the third lesson, is refunded at half the fee. After the third lesson no refund is made.

flags.clauseType: Attendance condition on the parent or guardian
flags.sourceSentence: A parent or guardian stays in the building for the whole lesson and watches from the viewing gallery rather than the poolside, so that the instructor has the pool edge clear.
flags.paragraph: A parent or guardian stays in the building for the whole lesson and watches from the viewing gallery rather than the poolside, so that the instructor has the pool edge clear.

verdicts.reason: The sentence is a twelve-month, fifteen-mile non-compete, and it stops the reader from working in their trade after the candidacy ends.
Meridian can change the rules, fees and terms just by posting them, which changes the reader's economics after they are committed.
Notice that arrives late leaves the reader owing dues for a whole further term.
This is a one-way indemnity that makes the reader pay third-party claims and legal fees; the counsel-selection detail is in the next sentence of the same paragraph.
The sentence is the automatic renewal at the then-current rate, the three-day window is in the same paragraph, and it locks the reader into further paid terms.
A suspended or medically held membership keeps renewing, so the reader can be committed to more dues while unable to use the club.
Meridian can raise dues on its own by at least six percent a year, which costs the reader money.
The authority covers only amounts owed and ends once the agreement is over and the balance is nil, so it is not open-ended and adds no cost beyond the charges themselves.
Program tuition renews automatically at whatever rate is then current, which commits the reader to paying a price they never agreed.
The reader gives up a jury trial and class actions unless they opt out in time, which is a right lost.
The late charge comes from a fee schedule Meridian can change, so the reader pays an amount the other side sets.
The Association refunds in proportion when it ends the licence, but the Plot Holder gets nothing back when they do, so the reader loses money on one side only.
Property left after the deadline goes to the Association, so the reader loses it.
Every claim, including lost work and revenue, is capped at one billing period's fee, which limits what the reader can recover.
Missing the thirty-day deadline commits the reader to another twelve months at whatever annual fee is then in effect.
Northwind can change the terms and pricing just by posting them, and continued use counts as acceptance.
Northwind can raise the fee on its own with notice, which costs the reader money.
The reader has to indemnify Northwind and pay its legal costs for third-party claims about their content.
The reader is forced into individual arbitration and loses class proceedings.
Unpaid amounts accrue 1.5 percent interest a month and reactivation costs a fee set in an external schedule, which costs the reader money.
A service credit is the only remedy for downtime, so the reader gives up any other remedy.
The cancellation takes effect at the end of the period already paid for, so the reader keeps the service they paid for and loses nothing.
Closing the account mid-period gives up the paid remainder of that period with no refund.
Northwind can suspend or close the reader's account for breaching Section 1, which takes away the service.
The account can be suspended on Northwind's belief alone, so the reader can lose access without any breach being shown.
This is a twelve-month non-compete that stops the reader working in their field whoever ends the employment.
Ardent can change policies, benefits and terms of employment without the reader's agreement.
The reader personally indemnifies Ardent for losses and attorney fees, including claims by a former employer.
The reader may not solicit colleagues or approach business contacts for a year, which limits what they can do after leaving.
The reader gives up a jury trial and class actions for employment claims, statutory claims included.
The full $15,000 has to be repaid if the reader leaves within twelve months.
The bonus may never be paid and is lost if the reader is not employed on the payment date.
Over unpaid charges the Operator can lock the reader out and sell their stored property.
The reader indemnifies the Operator and pays its attorney fees for claims brought by anyone.
Liability is capped at $5,000 even when the Operator is negligent, which limits what the reader can recover.
The Operator can change the agreement and rules by posting notice, which changes the reader's terms after they are committed.
The Operator can raise rent on its own with thirty days' notice.
The late and administration charges come from a schedule the Operator controls, and the reader pays them.
This sentence enforces the insurance obligation by putting all risk of loss on the reader.
The Operator can end the agreement without cause, which forces the reader to move their property out.
Applying payments to the oldest debt only pays amounts the reader already owes, and the sentence shows no extra cost.
The reader loses the unused part of the month's rent when they move out.
The Operator can enter the reader's unit without asking first, which is a right of privacy given up.
Cascade can change any term or charge on its own, which changes the reader's economics.
The reader indemnifies Cascade broadly, including for any charge on their account and for use by others.
Cancelling makes the whole device balance due at once, which costs the reader money immediately.
Liability is capped at one bill period's charges and lost data and profits are excluded, which limits what the reader can recover.
The reader gives up a jury trial and class actions.
Cascade can introduce or raise these non-government charges on its own with notice, which costs the reader money.
Late charges repeat every bill period and restoring a line costs a fee.
The reader pays for the full bill period after cancelling, with no proration.
The Firm can change the agreement's terms on its own by sending an email.
The Analyst indemnifies the Firm for losses and legal costs, including over anything they publish.
This is a six-month non-compete against listed firms plus a ban on approaching clients, which limits the reader's work.
The Firm can end the programme for any reason on one week's notice, which costs the reader the placement.
The Analyst gives up a jury trial and class actions.
Late instalments carry a charge set by the Firm's Handbook, which costs the reader money.
Items not returned are charged at a replacement cost the Firm sets, which costs the reader money.
The confidentiality duty has no end date, so the restriction on the reader lasts forever.
Keeping borrower records confidential protects other people and costs the volunteer nothing of substance.
Giving up a place late gets back only half the fee, which costs the reader money.
Watching from the viewing gallery is a harmless logistical condition that takes no money or meaningful right from the reader.
